paras.text: 19.53 per cent of our total national production is obtained from agriculture, but it is still being run on old methods; modern machines are not used; because of waterlogging and salinity the production of land is decreasing, and in our country the average production of one acre is low. Therefore, for increasing national income it is necessary that the system of farming be made better, agricultural reforms be enforced, and reform be made in all stages of sowing, harvesting and selling crops and moulding them into manufactures. 4. Agricultural development (Agricultural Development)

19.53 per cent of our total national production is obtained from agriculture, but it is still being run on old methods; modern machines are not used; because of waterlogging and salinity the production of land is decreasing, and in our country the average production of one acre is low. Therefore, for increasing national income it is necessary that the system of farming be made better, agricultural reforms be enforced, and reform be made in all stages of sowing, harvesting and selling crops and moulding them into manufactures. High-quality fertiliser and seed should be used; productivity (Productivity) in the agricultural sector should be increased; it is also necessary that diversification (Diversification) be created in agricultural production, i.e. different kinds of things, e.g. edible oil, sugarcane, vegetables, poultry, fish, meat and dairy products be increased; the use of agricultural machines be made popular, and modern agricultural technology be provided to small cultivators.

5. Industrial development

For the economic progress of Pakistan it is necessary that industries be developed and heavy industries (Heavy industry) (i.e. industries making machines for preparing different goods) be established, so that the speed of future economic progress becomes fast, and the necessary equipment can be obtained from within the country itself. At this time we import seventy per cent of our needed “investment goods” (Investment Goods) from foreign countries. The matters of importing machines from foreign countries and providing loans should be made easy, the system of taxes made better, and by ending tension in owner–labour relations conditions should be made pleasant.

6. Family planning (Family Planning)

Modern economists think that one reason for per capita income being low here is that the population is increasing rapidly, and the burden of population on the economic resources of the country is going on increasing. Therefore it is necessary that the speed of population growth be reduced. In Pakistan the campaign of family planning was begun in 1960.

At this time (in 2011) Pakistan, in terms of population, is the sixth largest country of the world (6th most populous country). According to the estimate of experts, if the population of Pakistan keeps growing at the present rate of increase, i.e. 2.05 per cent, then after thirty-nine years the total population will become double, from which very great pressure will fall on the country’s infrastructure (Infrastructure), e.g. houses, communications, electricity, water, sewerage, environmental cleanliness, and facilities of health and education etc.

7. Economic planning (Economic Planning)

For increasing national income it is necessary that the whole economy be made subject to a regulation; through economic planning, development programmes be made for agriculture, industry, trade, communications, banking and other sectors, and, giving them practical shape, the production of goods and services in the country be increased.

8. Just (Equitable) distribution of wealth

To increase per capita income it is also necessary that, as far as possible, national wealth be distributed in an equal and just way, because in this way, on one side, the problem of concentration of wealth will end, and enormous wealth will not accumulate with the wealthy class for it to squander in luxury and pleasure, and on the other side the middle and poor class too will have so much wealth that they will become able to take better advantage of their productive abilities, and thus an increase will occur in national income.

8. د شتمنۍ عادلانه (Equitable) وېش

د سړي سر عاید د زیاتولو لپاره دا هم اړینه ده چې تر وسې وسې هېوادنۍ شتمني په برابره او عادلانه توګه ووېشل شي، ځکه په دې ډول له یوې خوا د شتمنۍ د تمرکز ستونزه ختمېږي او د شتمنې طبقې سره به بې‌حسابه شتمني نه راټولېږي چې په عیش او عشرت کې یې والوزوي، او له بلې خوا به منځنۍ او غریبې طبقې ته هم دومره شتمني ورسېږي چې د خپلو تولیدي وړتیاوو څخه ښه ګټه پورته کړي، او په دې ډول به په ملي عاید کې زیاتوالی راشي.

4. Agricultural development (Agricultural Development)

19.53 per cent of our total national production is obtained from agriculture, but it is still being run on old methods; modern machines are not used; because of waterlogging and salinity the production of land is decreasing, and in our country the average production of one acre is low. Therefore, for increasing national income it is necessary that the system of farming be made better, agricultural reforms be enforced, and reform be made in all stages of sowing, harvesting and selling crops and moulding them into manufactures. High-quality fertiliser and seed should be used; productivity (Productivity) in the agricultural sector should be increased; it is also necessary that diversification (Diversification) be created in agricultural production, i.e. different kinds of things, e.g. edible oil, sugarcane, vegetables, poultry, fish, meat and dairy products be increased; the use of agricultural machines be made popular, and modern agricultural technology be provided to small cultivators.

5. Industrial development

For the economic progress of Pakistan it is necessary that industries be developed and heavy industries (Heavy industry) (i.e. industries making machines for preparing different goods) be established, so that the speed of future economic progress becomes fast, and the necessary equipment can be obtained from within the country itself. At this time we import seventy per cent of our needed “investment goods” (Investment Goods) from foreign countries. The matters of importing machines from foreign countries and providing loans should be made easy, the system of taxes made better, and by ending tension in owner–labour relations conditions should be made pleasant.

6. Family planning (Family Planning)

Modern economists think that one reason for per capita income being low here is that the population is increasing rapidly, and the burden of population on the economic resources of the country is going on increasing. Therefore it is necessary that the speed of population growth be reduced. In Pakistan the campaign of family planning was begun in 1960.

At this time (in 2011) Pakistan, in terms of population, is the sixth largest country of the world (6th most populous country). According to the estimate of experts, if the population of Pakistan keeps growing at the present rate of increase, i.e. 2.05 per cent, then after thirty-nine years the total population will become double, from which very great pressure will fall on the country’s infrastructure (Infrastructure), e.g. houses, communications, electricity, water, sewerage, environmental cleanliness, and facilities of health and education etc.

7. Economic planning (Economic Planning)

For increasing national income it is necessary that the whole economy be made subject to a regulation; through economic planning, development programmes be made for agriculture, industry, trade, communications, banking and other sectors, and, giving them practical shape, the production of goods and services in the country be increased.

8. Just (Equitable) distribution of wealth

To increase per capita income it is also necessary that, as far as possible, national wealth be distributed in an equal and just way, because in this way, on one side, the problem of concentration of wealth will end, and enormous wealth will not accumulate with the wealthy class for it to squander in luxury and pleasure, and on the other side the middle and poor class too will have so much wealth that they will become able to take better advantage of their productive abilities, and thus an increase will occur in national income.

4۔ زرعی ترقی: (Agricultural Development)

ہماری مجموعی قومی پیداوار کا 19.53 فیصد حصہ زراعت سے حاصل ہوتا ہے، لیکن ابھی تک یہ پرانے طریقوں پر چلائی جا رہی ہے، جدید طرز کی مشینوں کو استعمال نہیں کیا جاتا، سیم و تھور اور کٹاؤ کی وجہ سے زمین کی پیداوار گھٹتی جا رہی ہے اور ہمارے ملک میں، ایک ایکڑ کی اوسط پیداوار کم ہے، لہٰذا قومی آمدنی میں اضافہ کرنے کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ کھیتی باڑی کا نظام بہتر بنایا جائے، زرعی اصلاحات نافذ کی جائیں، فصلیں بونے، کاٹنے، فروخت کرنے اور مصنوعات میں ڈھالنے کے تمام مرحلوں میں اصلاح کی جائے۔ اعلیٰ کھاد اور بیج استعمال کرنے چاہئیں، زرعی شعبہ میں بار آوری (Productivity) بڑھانی چاہیے یہ بھی ضروری ہے کہ زرعی پیداوار میں تنوع (Diversification) پیدا کی جائے، یعنی مختلف قسم کی چیزیں، مثلاً خوردنی تیل، گنا، سبزیاں، پولٹری، مچھلی، گوشت اور ڈیری کی پیداواریں بڑھائی جائیں، زرعی مشینوں کا استعمال مقبول بنایا جائے اور چھوٹے کاشت کاروں کو جدید زرعی ٹیکنالوجی مہیا کی جائے۔

5۔ صنعتی ترقی:

پاکستان کی معاشی ترقی کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ صنعتوں کو ترقی دی جائے اور بھاری صنعتیں (Heavy industry) (یعنی مختلف اشیاء تیار کرنے کے لیے مشینیں بنانے والی صنعتیں) قائم کی جائیں تاکہ آئندہ معاشی ترقی کی رفتار تیز کرنے کے لیے ضروری ساز و سامان ملک کے اندر ہی سے مل سکے۔ اس وقت ہم اپنی ضرورت کی ”اشیائے سرمایہ کاری“ (Investment Goods) کا ستر فیصد غیر ممالک سے درآمد کرتے ہیں۔ غیر ممالک سے مشینوں کی درآمد اور قرضہ کی بہم رسانی کے امور سہل بنائے جائیں، ٹیکسوں کا نظام بہتر بنایا جائے، مالک اور مزدور کے تعلقات میں کشیدگی ختم کر کے حالات کو خوشگوار بنایا جائے۔

6۔ خاندانی منصوبہ بندی: (Family Planning)

جدید ماہرینِ معاشیات کا خیال ہے کہ ہمارے ہاں فی کس آمدنی کے پست ہونے کی ایک وجہ یہ ہے کہ آبادی تیزی سے بڑھ رہی ہے، اور ملک کے اقتصادی ذرائع پر آبادی کا بوجھ بڑھتا جا رہا ہے۔ اس لیے ضروری ہے کہ آبادی کے بڑھنے کی رفتار کم کی جائے۔ پاکستان میں خاندانی منصوبہ بندی کی مہم کا آغاز 1960ء میں کیا گیا تھا۔

اس وقت (2011ء میں) پاکستان آبادی کے لحاظ سے دنیا کا چھٹا بڑا ملک (6th most populous country) ہے۔ ماہرین کے اندازے کے مطابق اگر پاکستان کی آبادی موجودہ شرحِ اضافہ یعنی 2.05 فیصد شرح سے بڑھتی رہی تو اُنتالیس سال بعد کل آبادی دگنی ہو جائے گی، جس سے ملک کے تحتی ڈھانچہ (Infrastructure) پر بہت دباؤ پڑے گا۔ مثلاً مکانات، مواصلات، بجلی، پانی، نکاسیٔ آب، ماحولیاتی صفائی، صحت اور تعلیم کی سہولیات وغیرہ۔

7۔ اقتصادی منصوبہ بندی: (Economic Planning)

قومی آمدنی میں اضافہ کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ پوری معیشت کو ایک ضابطہ کا پابند بنایا جائے، معاشی منصوبہ بندی کے ذریعے زراعت، صنعت، تجارت، مواصلات، بنکاری اور دیگر شعبوں کے لیے ترقیاتی پروگرام بنائے جائیں اور انہیں عملی جامہ پہنا کر ملک میں اشیاء و خدمات کی پیداوار بڑھائی جائے۔

8۔ منصفانہ (Equitable) تقسیمِ دولت:

فی کس آمدنی بڑھانے کے لیے یہ بھی ضروری ہے کہ جس حد تک ممکن ہو، ملکی دولت مساویانہ اور منصفانہ طریقے سے تقسیم کی جائے، کیونکہ اس طرح ایک طرف تو ارتکازِ دولت کا مسئلہ ختم ہو جائے گا اور متمول طبقہ کے پاس اندھا دھند دولت جمع نہیں ہوگی کہ وہ اسے عیش و … (ص 129) … عشرت میں اڑائیں، اور دوسری طرف متوسط اور غریب طبقہ کے پاس بھی اتنی دولت آ جائے گی کہ وہ اپنی پیداواری صلاحیتوں سے بہتر فائدہ اٹھانے کے قابل ہو جائیں گے اور یوں قومی آمدنی میں اضافہ ہوگا۔

”اے ایمان والو! اسلام میں پورے کے پورے داخل ہو جاؤ!“ (البقرہ: 208) اس لیے موجودہ معاشی نظام میں اسلام کی پیوند کاری کرنے اور جزوی طور پر بعض اسلامی قوانین نافذ کرنے کی بجائے پورے اجتماعی، معاشرتی، سیاسی اور معاشی نظام کو اسلامی نظامِ حیات میں ڈھال دینا چاہیے۔

The command of Allah Almighty is:

Translation: “So that it (wealth) does not merely circulate among your rich ones.” (Surah Al-Hashr 59:7)

9. Economic system of Islam (Islamic Economic System)

If the complete economic system of Islam is enforced in Pakistan, then whatever basic shortcomings are found in our economy will all end, and the economy will be established on strong and stable foundations, because in it such institutions are established which create a beautiful balance and moderation in the economy, e.g. zakat, ushr, sadaqat, qard-e-hasan, mudarabah, distinction of halal and haram, obstacles to concentration of wealth, abolition of interest, ending exploitation, the right of the needy and deprived, honesty and trustworthiness, simplicity and frugality, and the prohibition of extravagance. In such conditions national income increases, and class discrimination too cannot arise conspicuously. The command of Allah Almighty is:

“O you who believe! Enter into Islam completely.” (Al-Baqarah 2:208) Therefore, instead of grafting Islam onto the present economic system and enforcing some Islamic laws partially, the entire collective, social, political and economic system should be moulded into the Islamic system of life.
